video_goal: Demonstrate how to efficiently and accurately count a retail cash drawer using the AccuBANKER AB-5000 bill counter.
required_subjects_and_props: AccuBANKER AB-5000 bill counter, retail cash drawer (till), mixed denomination US dollar bills, tally sheet, pen

outline_steps.visual_action: A hand flips the rear power switch of the AccuBANKER AB-5000, causing the front LCD screen to illuminate with a blue backlight.
Two hands lift a black plastic cash drawer filled with sorted bills and coins, placing it on the desk directly to the left of the bill counter.
An index finger presses the 'MODE' button on the AccuBANKER AB-5000 control panel until the word 'MIX' appears on the digital display.
A hand reaches into the far-right compartment of the cash drawer, lifting the metal spring clip, and pulls out a thick stack of $1 bills.
Two hands tap the long and short edges of the $1 bill stack against the flat desk surface to align all the bills perfectly.
The hand places the aligned stack of bills into the top hopper of the AccuBANKER AB-5000, sliding them back to trigger the feed sensor.
The rubber rollers of the AB-5000 spin rapidly, pulling the bills one by one from the top hopper and feeding them down into the bottom stacker.
The AB-5000 LCD screen numbers tick up rapidly, stopping to display a final piece count of '45' and a total value of '$45'.
A hand grasps the neatly stacked $1 bills from the bottom stacker and pulls them completely out of the machine.
A hand holding a pen writes the number '45.00' on the '$1' line of a paper cash drawer tally sheet resting on the desk.
The hand reaches back into the cash drawer, lifts the second metal clip, and pulls out a stack of $5 bills.
The hand drops the squared $5 bills into the top hopper of the AccuBANKER AB-5000, and the rollers immediately begin spinning to count the new stack.
